                                                          Abstract
      Offline policy learning (OPL) usually optimizes the mean of a scalar potential outcome (Kitagawa
      and Tetenov, 2018; Athey and Wager, 2021). We study OPL when each potential outcome is a
      probability measure: for each action a ∈ A, Y[a] ∈ P2 (R). From logged data {(Xi , Ai , Yi )}Ni=1
      collected under propensity f0 (a | x), and under standard causal assumptions, a policy π : X → A
      induces Y[π(X)]. We evaluate it by a Wasserstein-Lipschitz utility of its barycenter,
